about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice B): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Apple Pie Slab Squares
recipes.summary: A buttery pastry slab filled with cinnamon apples and topped with a crumb, cut into hand-held squares.
steps: Rub the flour, butter and icing sugar into fine crumbs, add the egg yolk and water and press into a dough. Wrap and chill until firm.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Line a 20cm by 30cm tin with baking paper.
Cook the apples, brown sugar, cinnamon, cornflour and lemon juice in a pan for 8 minutes until the apples are just tender, then cool.
Press two thirds of the dough into the tin, spread with the apples and crumble the remaining dough over the top.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until the top is golden and the filling bubbles at the edges. Cool in the tin, then cut into 12 squares.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough.
Storage: keeps 3 days in an airtight container; refrigerate in hot weather.

recipes.title: Lemon Meringue Tartlets
recipes.summary: Crisp sweet pastry cases with a tangy lemon curd and a toasted meringue peak.
steps: Rub the flour, butter and icing sugar into crumbs, mix in the 1 yolk and water to a dough, wrap and chill until firm.

Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Roll out the dough, cut 12 rounds and press into a 12-hole muffin tin. Prick, line with paper and baking beans, and blind bake for 12 minutes, then remove the paper and bake 5 minutes more until pale gold.
Whisk the 3 yolks, 100g sugar, zest, juice, butter and cornflour in a saucepan over medium heat for 5 minutes until thick, then divide between the cases.
Whisk the egg whites to soft peaks, add the 150g sugar a spoonful at a time and whisk until stiff and glossy. Pipe or spoon onto the tartlets.
Bake at 150°C fan (170°C conventional) for 8 minutes until the meringue peaks are golden. Cool in the tin.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough.
Storage: best the day they are made; keep in the fridge for up to 2 days.

recipes.title: Portuguese-Style Custard Tartlets
recipes.summary: Flaky puff pastry cups holding a vanilla custard with dark blistered tops.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C fan (240°C conventional). Roll the pastry sheet into a tight log, slice into 12 rounds and press each into a greased 12-hole muffin tin, thinning the base and pushing the pastry up the sides.
Whisk the cornflour with a little of the milk, then heat the rest of the milk, cream, sugar and lemon zest in a pan until steaming. Whisk in the cornflour mixture and stir for 3 minutes until thick.
Whisk a little hot custard into the yolks, then stir back into the pan with the vanilla. Remove the zest and cool for 5 minutes.
Spoon the custard into the pastry cases.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes until the pastry is golden and the custard tops are blistered and dark in patches. Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then on a rack.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 tartlet.
Storage: eat within 2 days; refresh in a hot oven for 4 minutes.

recipes.title: Treacle Tart Wedges
recipes.summary: Golden syrup and breadcrumb filling in a crisp sweet pastry, balanced with lemon.
steps: Rub the flour, butter and icing sugar into crumbs, mix in the yolk and water, wrap and chill until firm.

Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Roll out the dough to line a 23cm tart tin, prick the base, line with paper and baking beans and blind bake for 12 minutes, then remove the paper and beans.
Warm the golden syrup until runny, stir in the breadcrumbs, zest, juice and egg.
Pour into the pastry case and bake for 25 minutes until set at the edges and golden. Cool in the tin and cut into 12 wedges.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough.
Food safety: bake until the egg filling is fully set, with no liquid centre, and reaches 75°C in the middle.
Storage: keeps 4 days in an airtight container; serve with cream if wanted.

recipes.title: Bakewell Tart Slices
recipes.summary: Jam and almond frangipane in a sweet pastry case with flaked almonds on top.
steps: Rub the 200g flour, cold butter and icing sugar into crumbs, mix in the yolk and water, wrap and chill until firm.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Line a 23cm tart tin with the rolled dough, prick, line with paper and baking beans and blind bake for 12 minutes, then remove the paper.
Spread the jam over the base. Beat the softened butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs, almond meal and 25g flour.
Spoon the frangipane over the jam, level it and scatter with the sliced almonds.
Bake for 30 minutes until puffed, golden and firm in the middle. Cool in the tin and cut into 12 slices.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts, gluten, milk and egg. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough.
Storage: keeps 4 days in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Chocolate Ganache Tartlets
recipes.summary: Crisp cocoa pastry cases filled with a silky dark chocolate ganache.
steps: Rub the flour, cocoa, butter and icing sugar into crumbs, mix in the yolk and water, wrap and chill until firm.

Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Roll out and cut 12 rounds to line a 12-hole muffin tin. Prick, line with paper and baking beans and bake for 12 minutes, then remove the paper and bake 5 minutes more. Cool.
Heat the cream with the honey and salt until steaming and pour over the broken chocolate. Stand for 2 minutes, then stir until glossy.
Divide the ganache between the cases and chill until set.
Remove from the tin and serve at room temperature.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough and 1 hour setting the ganache.
Storage: keeps 3 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Maple Walnut Tart Squares
recipes.summary: A gooey maple and walnut filling over a buttery shortbread-style base.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Rub the flour, cold butter and caster sugar into crumbs, mix in the yolk and press firmly into the tin. Bake for 15 minutes until pale gold.
Whisk the eggs, maple syrup, brown sugar, melted butter and vanilla until smooth, then stir in the walnuts.
Pour over the base and bake for 25 minutes until just set with a slight wobble in the middle.
Cool completely in the tin, then cut into 12 squares.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts, gluten, milk and egg.
Food safety: bake until the egg filling is fully set, with no liquid centre, and reaches 75°C in the middle.
Storage: keeps 4 days in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Pear and Almond Frangipane Tartlets
recipes.summary: Small tarts with almond cream and poached pear slices, glazed with warm apricot jam.
steps: Rub the flour, cold butter and icing sugar into crumbs, mix in the yolk and water, wrap and chill until firm.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Roll out and cut 12 rounds to line a 12-hole muffin tin and prick the bases.
Beat the softened butter and caster sugar until pale, then beat in the egg and almond meal.
Spoon the almond cream into the cases and top each with 3 or 4 pear slices.
Bake for 28 to 30 minutes until the pastry and almond cream are golden. Warm the jam with 1 tbsp water, brush over the warm tartlets and cool in the tin.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts, gluten, milk and egg. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough.
Storage: best within 2 days; keep covered in a cool place.

recipes.title: Orange Almond Tart Slices
recipes.summary: A sweet pastry tart with a fragrant orange and almond filling.
steps: Rub the flour, cold butter and icing sugar into crumbs, mix in the yolk and water, wrap and chill until firm.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Line a 23cm tart tin with the rolled dough, prick, line with paper and baking beans and blind bake for 12 minutes, then remove the paper.
Whisk the eggs and sugar for 3 minutes until pale. Fold in the almond meal, zest, juice and rose water.
Pour into the pastry case, scatter with the sliced almonds and bake for 28 minutes until golden and set.
Cool in the tin and cut into 12 slices.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts, gluten, milk and egg. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough.
Storage: keeps 3 days in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Oat Apple Pie Bars
recipes.summary: An oat crumble base and topping around spiced apple filling, no pastry rolling needed.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Mix the oats, flour, sugar, first cinnamon, baking powder and melted butter into a crumbly dough.
Press two thirds into the tin and bake for 10 minutes.
Toss the apples with the lemon juice, cornflour and remaining cinnamon, spread over the base and scatter with the remaining crumble.
Bake for 30 minutes until golden and the apples are tender. Cool completely in the tin and cut into 12 bars.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 bar.
Storage: keeps 4 days in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Pie Squares
recipes.summary: Spiced pumpkin custard on a shortbread base, cut into neat squares.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Rub the flour, butter and icing sugar into crumbs, press into the tin and bake for 15 minutes until pale gold.
Whisk the pumpkin, eggs, sugar, cream and spices until smooth and pour over the base.
Bake for 35 minutes until set with a slight wobble in the centre and the edges are dry.
Cool in the tin, chill, then cut into 12 squares.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus 2 hours chilling before cutting.
Storage: keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.

recipes.title: Sweet Potato Pie Bars
recipes.summary: Creamy spiced sweet potato filling over an oat and pecan base.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Mix the oats, flour, pecans, melted butter and brown sugar and press into the tin. Bake for 12 minutes.
Whisk the sweet potato, eggs, milk, maple syrup and cinnamon until smooth and pour over the base.
Bake for 35 minutes until set with a slight wobble in the middle.
Cool, chill until firm, then cut into 12 bars.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts, gluten, milk and egg. Plus 2 hours chilling before cutting.
Storage: keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.

recipes.title: Lime Pie Squares
recipes.summary: A tangy lime custard on a crisp oat base, light and refreshing.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Mix the oats, flour, melted butter and brown sugar and press into the tin. Bake for 12 minutes until golden.
Whisk the egg yolks, condensed milk, lime zest and juice until thick and pour over the warm base.
Bake for 12 minutes until just set with a slight wobble. Cool, then chill until firm.
Whip the cream with the icing sugar, spread over the top and cut into 12 squares.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus 3 hours chilling before cutting.
Food safety: bake until the egg filling is fully set, with no liquid centre, and reaches 75°C in the middle.
Storage: keep in the fridge for up to 3 days.

recipes.title: Caramel Pecan Tartlets
recipes.summary: Crisp pastry cases filled with a buttery caramel and toasted pecans.
steps: Rub the flour, cold butter and icing sugar into crumbs, mix in the yolk and water, wrap and chill until firm.

Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Roll out and cut 12 rounds to line a 12-hole muffin tin. Prick, line with paper and baking beans and bake for 12 minutes, then remove the paper and bake 5 minutes more.
Boil the sugar, butter, golden syrup and cream for 3 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy. Stir in the pecans.
Spoon into the cases and bake for 8 minutes until bubbling. Cool in the tin until the caramel is firm.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts, gluten, milk and egg. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough.
Storage: keeps 4 days in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Jam Tart Bars
recipes.summary: A shortbread base and crumb topping around a layer of apricot jam, like a jam tart in bar form.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Rub the flour, baking powder, butter and sugar into crumbs, then mix in the egg, yolk and vanilla to a soft dough.
Press two thirds into the tin, spread with the jam and crumble the rest over, scattering with the coconut.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until golden. Cool completely in the tin and cut into 12 bars.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 bar.
Storage: keeps 5 days in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Apricot Coconut Slice
recipes.summary: A chewy oat and coconut slice layered with apricot jam.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Mix the flour, oats, 80g coconut, sugar and melted butter. Press two thirds into the tin.
Spread with the jam. Mix the egg into the remaining mixture, crumble it over the jam and scatter with the 30g coconut.
Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until golden. Cool in the tin and cut into 12 pieces.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 piece.
Storage: keeps 5 days in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Butterscotch Blondie Squares
recipes.summary: Chewy brown sugar blondies with a butterscotch flavour and chopped pecans.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Whisk the melted butter and sugar until smooth, then whisk in the eggs and vanilla.
Fold in the flour, baking powder, salt and pecans until just combined and spread into the tin.
Bake for 25 to 28 minutes until the top is crackled and golden, and the centre is just set. Cool in the tin and cut into 12 squares.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts, gluten, milk and egg.
Food safety: bake until the egg filling is fully set, with no liquid centre, and reaches 75°C in the middle.
Storage: keeps 4 days in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Millionaire-Style Shortbread Squares
recipes.summary: Shortbread topped with a soft condensed milk caramel and dark chocolate.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Rub the flour, cold butter and caster sugar together until it clumps, press into the tin and bake for 20 minutes until pale gold.
Heat the 100g butter, brown sugar, condensed milk and golden syrup over medium heat for 8 minutes, stirring constantly, until thick and caramel coloured.
Pour over the shortbread and cool.
Melt the chocolate, spread over the caramel and chill until set, then cut into 12 squares with a hot knife.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus 1 hour setting.
Storage: keeps 5 days in the fridge in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Cream Cheese Brownie Swirls
recipes.summary: Fudgy chocolate brownies marbled with a tangy cream cheese swirl.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Melt the butter and chocolate together and cool slightly. Whisk in the 150g sugar and the eggs, then fold in the flour and cocoa.
Beat the cream cheese, 40g sugar and yolk until smooth.
Spread the brownie batter in the tin, dollop the cream cheese mixture on top and drag a knife through to swirl.
Bake for 32 to 35 minutes until the edges are set and the centre has a slight wobble. Cool in the tin and cut into 12 squares.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 square.
Storage: keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.

recipes.title: Sugar-Reduced Chocolate Brownies
recipes.summary: Rich brownies using about half the sugar of a classic recipe, with apple sauce for moisture.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Melt the chocolate and butter, stir smooth and cool slightly.
Whisk in the eggs, sugar, apple sauce and vanilla, then fold in the flour, cocoa and baking powder.
Spread into the tin and bake for 22 to 25 minutes until the top is set and a skewer comes out with a few moist crumbs.
Cool in the tin and cut into 12 squares.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. About 8g sugar a brownie, against 18g in a classic one.
Storage: keeps 4 days in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Black Bean Brownies
recipes.summary: Fudgy brownies blended with black beans for fibre and moisture, and no flour.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Blend the beans, eggs, oil, sugar, cocoa, vanilla and baking powder until completely smooth.
Stir in half the chocolate, spread into the tin and scatter with the rest.
Bake for 25 to 28 minutes until the top is set and a skewer comes out with a few moist crumbs.
Cool completely in the tin before cutting into 12 squares, as they firm up as they cool.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Gluten free if the baking powder is gluten free.
Storage: keep in the fridge for up to 5 days.

recipes.title: Chickpea Blondies
recipes.summary: Soft blondies made from blended chickpeas, with a nutty butterscotch flavour.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Blend the chickpeas, eggs, peanut butter, sugar, vanilla, baking powder and salt until completely smooth.
Stir in half the chocolate, spread into the tin and scatter with the rest.
Bake for 25 to 28 minutes until golden and set in the centre. Cool completely in the tin and cut into 12 squares.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains peanuts, gluten, milk, egg and soy. Gluten free if the baking powder is gluten free.
Storage: keep in the fridge for up to 5 days.

recipes.title: Dutch Baby Wedges
recipes.summary: A puffed oven pancake baked in a hot pan, dusted with cinnamon sugar and cut into wedges.
steps: Heat the oven to 210°C fan (230°C conventional) with a 25cm ovenproof frying pan inside.
Blend the eggs, milk, flour, 1 tbsp sugar, salt and vanilla until smooth.
Add the butter to the hot pan until it melts and foams, swirl to coat, then pour in the batter.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until puffed and deep golden at the edges. Dust with the cinnamon and remaining sugar, then cut into 8 wedges and serve straight away.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 wedge. It deflates as it cools, which is normal.
Storage: best eaten warm.

recipes.title: Scottish Shortbread Rounds
recipes.summary: Buttery, crumbly shortbread with only three ingredients and a hint of salt.
steps: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional). Line two trays with baking paper.
Beat the butter and 100g sugar until pale, then work in the flour and salt to a soft dough.
Roll out to 1cm thick, cut 12 rounds with a 6cm cutter and place on the trays. Prick with a fork.
Bake for 20 minutes until pale gold and just firm. Sprinkle with the remaining sugar while hot and cool on the tray.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 round.
Storage: keeps 2 weeks in an airtight tin.

recipes.title: Clafoutis Squares
recipes.summary: A baked custard batter around soft apple, cut into squares and served warm or cold.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Grease a 20cm by 30cm baking dish.
Fry the apples in the butter for 5 minutes until just soft and arrange in the dish.
Whisk the eggs and sugar, then whisk in the flour, milk, cream and vanilla until smooth.
Pour over the apples and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until puffed, golden and set.
Dust with the icing sugar, cool for 10 minutes and cut into 12 squares.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 square.
Storage: best the day it is made; keep in the fridge for 2 days.
